title: Integrated multi-omics and molecular docking reveal shared molecular mechanisms of Helicobacter pylori infection and rheumatic diseases.
authors: Cai, Ting; Zhao, Xuelin; Hu, Hai; Wang, Fen; Zhang, Minglin
one_liner_zh: 该文通过多组学与分子对接研究幽门螺杆菌与风湿病共享机制，虽涉及转录因子预测和分子对接，但核心是疾病关联而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法深度有限。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ), a Group 1 carcinogen, is linked to gastritis, gastric cancer, and extragastric diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), primary Sjogren syndrome (pSS), and systemic sclerosis (SSc). Despite these epidemiological associations, the molecular mechanisms underlying their comorbidity remain unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Integrated transcriptomics were used to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) shared between H. pylori and rheumatic diseases, functional enrichment analysis and molecular docking were performed, and hub genes, predicted regulatory transcription factors, and small-molecule drugs were identified. RESULTS: We identified DEGs shared between H. pylori infection and rheumatic diseases, namely 134 (RA), 103 (SLE), 244 (pSS), and 75 (SSc). Functional enrichment revealed the following convergent pathways across diseases: immune activation (in RA and pSS), viral defense (in SLE and SSc), and dysregulated Toll-like/NOD-like receptor signaling. Based on the highest degree scores, hub gene screening prioritized CXCL10, JUN (RA); STAT1, CXCL10, ISG15, and MX1 (SLE); PTPRC, ITGB2, CD19, STAT1, and CXCL10 (pSS); and STAT1, CXCL10, MX1, and OAS1 (SSc). Immune infiltration demonstrated disease-specific dysregulation: M1 macrophages in RA/pSS, monocytes in SLE, and T-cell subsets in SSc. Transcription factor analysis revealed STAT1, RELA, and IRFs to be key regulators, as validated in disease datasets. Drug prediction and molecular docking revealed geldanamycin (targeting IGF1R and JUN in RA), oestriol (OAS family and ISG15 in SLE), atorvastatin (CXCL10 and TLR4 in pSS), and cerivastatin ( TLR4 in SSc) as potential therapeutics. CONCLUSION: This study revealed the immune/viral pathways and hub genes linking H. pylori to rheumatic diseases, suggesting potential therapeutic targets.
abstract_zh: 背景：幽门螺杆菌（Helicobacter pylori, H. pylori）作为一类致癌物，与胃炎、胃癌及胃外疾病相关，包括类风湿关节炎（RA）、系统性红斑狼疮（SLE）、原发性干燥综合征（pSS）和系统性硬化症（SSc）。尽管存在这些流行病学关联，但其共病背后的分子机制仍不清楚。材料与方法：采用整合转录组学方法鉴定H. pylori与风湿性疾病共享的差异表达基因（DEGs），进行功能富集分析和分子对接，并识别枢纽基因、预测调控转录因子及小分子药物。结果：我们鉴定了H. pylori感染与风湿性疾病共享的DEGs，分别为134个（RA）、103个（SLE）、244个（pSS）和75个（SSc）。功能富集揭示了以下跨疾病的趋同通路：免疫激活（在RA和pSS中）、病毒防御（在SLE和SSc中）以及失调的Toll样/NOD样受体信号传导。基于最高度值评分，枢纽基因筛选优先考虑了CXCL10、JUN（RA）；STAT1、CXCL10、ISG15和MX1（SLE）；PTPRC、ITGB2、CD19、STAT1和CXCL10（pSS）；以及STAT1、CXCL10、MX1和OAS1（SSc）。免疫浸润显示疾病特异性失调：RA/pSS中的M1巨噬细胞、SLE中的单核细胞以及SSc中的T细胞亚群。转录因子分析揭示STAT1、RELA和IRFs是关键调控因子，并在疾病数据集中得到验证。药物预测和分子对接显示，格尔德霉素（靶向RA中的IGF1R和JUN）、雌三醇（SLE中的OAS家族和ISG15）、阿托伐他汀（pSS中的CXCL10和TLR4）和西立伐他汀（SSc中的TLR4）为潜在治疗药物。结论：本研究揭示了连接H. pylori与风湿性疾病的免疫/病毒通路及枢纽基因，提示了潜在的治疗靶点。
